claims.statement: Shared practices, expectations, sanctions, roles and artefacts can reduce individual cognitive and coordination work required to identify situations and select action.
claims.rival: Incentives, information and repeated interaction fully explain the effect.

claims.statement: Empirical expectations, normative expectations, sanction expectations, personal endorsement and observed conformity are distinct norm components with potentially separable behavioural effects.
claims.rival: Reported expectations rationalize incentive-driven behaviour or demand effects.

claims.statement: Formal rules and participant culture can influence one another over time after migration and composition are modelled separately.
claims.rival: Institution-culture association is sorting by participant preference.

claims.statement: Communication-network structure and scale can filter diverse classifications into stable shared categories for bounded tasks.
claims.rival: Convergence is produced by stimulus salience or task demand.

claims.statement: Category, reporting, standing and aggregation rules alter which experiences enter institutional records and decisions.
claims.rival: Differences reflect signal quality, privacy, expertise or decision cost.

claims.statement: Institutions are presumptively defective when systematically affected parties lack proportionate standing to contest consequential classifications.
claims.rival: Expanded standing can reduce decision quality, privacy or legitimate expertise.

claims.statement: Preregistered transformation families recur above generic-narrative, corpus-composition, descent, borrowing and coder-template controls in independently coded held-out myth corpora.
claims.rival: Apparent recurrence is generic story structure, transmission history, archive bias or flexible coding.

claims.statement: Common descent, borrowing, convergence, genre constraint, archive selection and coder abstraction make distinguishable contributions to detected recurrence.
claims.rival: The available corpus cannot identify these contributions separately.

sources.use: norm-component measurement and long-term experimental change

sources.limit: online communities with low migration cost

sources.limit: novel ambiguous stimuli and US online participants
